{
  "findings": [
    {
      "id": "F1",
      "priority": "P2",
      "title": "PhotoSwipe gallery fails to open if any image in the set has no intrinsic dimensions (e.g., broken link)",
      "file": "app/photo-gallery.mjs",
      "lines": "5-18, 21-24",
      "mechanism": "`showPhotoGallery` awaits `Promise.all(items.map(item => imageSize(item.src)...))`. The `imageSize` function rejects if `image.naturalWidth` or `naturalHeight` is 0. If one photo in a trip's gallery is broken/missing, the entire `Promise.all` rejects. This triggers the `catch` block in `openGallery` (main.mjs:198), which falls back to the simple `<dialog>` viewer showing only the clicked image, rather than opening the full PhotoSwipe gallery with navigation.",
      "reproduction": "1. In API mode, add multiple photos to a trip.\n2. Manually corrupt or delete one of the stored media files on disk so it returns 404 or renders as 0x0.\n3. Click a valid photo thumbnail in the UI.\n4. Observe that the full-screen PhotoSwipe gallery does not open; instead, a basic modal opens for just that one image.",
      "fix": "In `photo-gallery.mjs`, change `Promise.all` to `Promise.allSettled`. Map over the results, using `{width: 1600, height: 1200}` (or similar default) for rejected promises, ensuring the gallery always initializes.",
      "confidence": "High"
    },
    {
      "id": "F2",
      "priority": "P2",
      "title": "Desktop map markers and labels may overlap/clipping at specific zoom levels due to fixed pixel scaling logic",
      "file": "app/main.mjs",
      "lines": "115-131",
      "mechanism": "The SVG marker rendering calculates `pixelsPerUnit` based on the container size and current view width. It then scales marker radius (`r`) and font sizes by this factor. However, the positioning logic for text labels (`rightEdge` check) uses a hardcoded character-width approximation (`city.name.length * .6`). At certain desktop widths (e.g., 1280px) and zoom levels, this approximation can fail, causing long city names to extend beyond the viewport or overlap adjacent markers, especially when `view.width` is small but `rect.width` is large.",
      "reproduction": "1. Set browser window to ~1280x720.\n2. Load the app in Demo mode.\n3. Zoom into a cluster of cities (e.g., Japan region).\n4. Observe if city labels (like 'Sapporo' or 'Tokyo') clip off the edge of the map panel or overlap other markers significantly.",
      "fix": "Use `getComputedTextLength()` on the SVG text element after appending it to adjust its position dynamically, or implement a collision detection algorithm for labels. Alternatively, hide labels below a certain zoom threshold where overlap is guaranteed.",
      "confidence": "Medium"
    },
    {
      "id": "F3",
      "priority": "P2",
      "title": "Composer draft persistence race condition on rapid city switching",
      "file": "app/main.mjs",
      "lines": "13-17, 202-214",
      "mechanism": "When switching cities rapidly, `renderMemories` creates new composer forms. The `composerDraft` function reads from `sessionStorage`. If a user types in City A, switches to City B, then quickly switches back to City A before the `input` event handler for City B finishes saving its empty state (or if the save operation is throttled/debounced incorrectly), there is a risk of overwriting City A's draft with an empty object or stale data because `saveComposerDraft` writes the entire `composerDrafts` object back to storage. While `sessionStorage` is synchronous, the DOM manipulation and event listener attachment happen asynchronously enough that a fast tab-switch could theoretically read a partially updated state if the previous form's cleanup didn't run.",
      "reproduction": "Hard to reproduce reliably without artificial delay injection, but possible on low-power devices. Type text in Composer A. Switch to City B. Immediately switch back to City A. Check if text persists.",
      "fix": "Ensure `clearComposerDraft` or `saveComposerDraft` is called explicitly on form unmount/cleanup if possible, or use a more granular key structure in sessionStorage to avoid whole-object rewrites during rapid interactions.",
      "confidence": "Low"
    },
    {
      "id": "F4",
      "priority": "P3",
      "title": "Accessibility: Focus trap in PhotoSwipe might conflict with browser native focus behavior on some desktop setups",
      "file": "app/photo-gallery.mjs",
      "lines": "46-50",
      "mechanism": "The code sets `document.querySelector('.topbar').inert = true` and `main.inert = true` when the gallery opens. While this prevents interaction with background elements, it also removes them from the accessibility tree. When the gallery closes, it restores `priorInert`. If the `destroy` event fires unexpectedly or if there's an error during initialization, the `inert` attribute might remain set, locking the user out of the main application interface until reload.",
      "reproduction": "1. Open PhotoSwipe gallery.\n2. Force an error in the console during gallery init (simulate network failure for library load).\n3. Check if `.topbar` and `main` remain `inert=true`.",
      "fix": "Add a global error boundary or ensure `inert` restoration happens in a `finally` block or via a MutationObserver fallback if the standard `destroy` event doesn't fire.",
      "confidence": "Medium"
    },
    {
      "id": "F5",
      "priority": "P3",
      "title": "CSS: Album view grid layout may cause horizontal scrolling on narrow desktop windows (<1024px)",
      "file": "app/styles.css",
      "lines": "8, 11",
      "mechanism": "In album view, `.workspace` changes to `grid-template-columns: 264px minmax(0, 1fr)`. The memory panel has `padding: 36px 40px`. On screens between 851px and 1024px, the combination of the fixed sidebar width and the padding might force the content area to be very narrow, potentially causing internal elements (like trip cards with images) to overflow their containers if `min-width: 0` isn't strictly enforced on all nested flex/grid children.",
      "reproduction": "1. Resize browser to 900px width.\n2. Switch to Album view.\n3. Add a trip with a wide cover image.\n4. Check for horizontal scrollbar on the body or memory panel.",
      "fix": "Verify `overflow-x: hidden` on `.memory-panel` or ensure all child elements have `min-width: 0` and `max-width: 100%`.",
      "confidence": "Low"
    }
  ],
  "unverified_hypotheses": [
    {
      "title": "Potential XSS via malformed GeoJSON properties",
      "description": "The app loads `city-regions.geojson`. If this file were compromised or malformed, `feature.properties.city_id` is used in `data-city-id` attributes. While `textContent` is used for most things, `setAttribute` is used for IDs. If `city_id` contained malicious characters, it could break HTML parsing. However, since this is local/static data, risk is negligible unless the build process is compromised."
    },
    {
      "title": "Memory leak in DraftStore",
      "description": "The `DraftStore` keeps references to DOM elements? No, it stores strings. But `editCard` attaches listeners. If `renderMemories` is called frequently, old forms are removed via `replaceChildren`. Listeners should be garbage collected. Unlikely to be a major issue but worth monitoring in long sessions."
    }
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "No runtime execution was performed; findings are based on static analysis of the provided source code.",
    "Visual overlap issues (F2) depend heavily on specific font metrics and browser rendering engines which cannot be perfectly predicted statically.",
    "Security assumptions rely on the threat model provided (local backend, trusted static frontend). If the GitHub Pages deployment serves different data, risks change.",
    "Performance implications of `structuredClone` in `DemoRepository` on large datasets were not measured."
  ]
}
